title: A Provision for the Trail
premise: Mara Halloran, captain of the riverboat Kestrel, has spent seven years outrunning a warrant from the drowned Republic of Vessia, moving cargo up and down the Sable River because every port remembers her face. When the monsoon flood delivers a chest bearing the Vessian seal — and inside it, proof that the man who betrayed her crew is still alive and buying loyalty — she is dragged back toward the capital she fled, aided by Tomas Vey, a quiet salvager with his own debts to the old regime. As the river drops toward the dry season and the Kestrel takes damage she cannot afford to fix, Mara must choose between the truth that would clear her name and the loyalty that kept her crew's memory sacred. In the end she surrenders the chest to the Vessian tribunal, testifies against the traitor, and loses the boat — but gains a pardon, Tomas's partnership, and the first port she's allowed herself to stop in.
about_author: Zephyrine Brightwater is the pen name of a former barge-hand turned novelist who spent a decade working inland waterways before trading the river for the writing desk. She lives in a houseboat she refuses to name, and writes adventure stories about people who can't afford to stop moving.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A routine cargo run down the Sable River establishes Mara's mastery of the water and her refusal to dock at Vessia's old capital, skirting questions from her deckhand Odile. Emotional beat: competence as armor — Mara reads the river perfectly but can't read her own past without flinching.

chapters.title: What the Flood Brings Up
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Monsoon rains swell the river; the Kestrel's crew salvages a waterlogged chest stamped with the Vessian seal wedged in a sandbar. Inside are sealed dispatches and a manifest listing crew names Mara recognizes — including her own. Beat: dread; the past has literally surfaced.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Levee
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Salvager Tomas Vey recognizes the chest at a trading post and follows the Kestrel downstream, offering help with her leaking hull in exchange for a look inside. Mara refuses. Beat: wary friction; two survivors of the same drowned country circling each other.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Sandbars
chapters.summary: POV Mara, flashback woven through a night anchor. We learn of the Vessian collapse, the crew Mara lost when someone sold their smuggling route to the regime's hunters, and the warrant that keeps her moving. Beat: grief revealed; the chest is a key to a wound.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The Kestrel's hull seam splits in debris-choked water; Odile sends word to Tomas, who arrives and helps patch her at a derelict lock. Mara, furious, lets him stay one night. Beat: reluctant interdependence; the boat is failing just as her control is.

chapters.title: Dispatches from a Dead Nation
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Tomas reveals he was a Vessian archivist; the chest holds orders proving the crew's betrayal was bought by a man named Corvel Sarn — the tribunal's new star witness, now a respectable trader. Beat: revelation and rage; the traitor is thriving.

chapters.title: Port of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV Mara. At Greyharbor, Mara learns Sarn has put a quiet price on the chest — and on her. Odile urges her to sink it and run. Beat: temptation of forgetting versus the pull of the crew's names.

chapters.title: The Man Who Bought Loyalty
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Tomas confronts his own complicity: as an archivist he processed the very orders that doomed Mara's crew and stayed silent. He confesses to her. Beat: betrayal within the alliance; loyalty and truth begin to war openly.

chapters.title: Dry Season Coming
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The river drops; low water means the Kestrel can't make the upstream run to the tribunal seat at Vessel's Rest before channels close. Mara must decide in days, not weeks. Beat: the clock tightens; survival and justice now compete for the same narrow water.

chapters.title: Sarn's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Sarn's agent offers Mara a pardon and a new boat if she sells the chest and names Tomas as the leak's source. Beat: the devil's arithmetic — everything she wants, bought with someone else's neck.

chapters.title: What Odile Knows
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile admits she's been reporting Mara's movements to Greyharbor harbor-masters for years — not for Sarn, but to keep bounty hunters off the boat, a small treachery done out of loyalty. Beat: the theme crystallized; love and lies entangled.

chapters.title: Night Run
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Mara, Odile, and Tomas run the Kestrel through a moonless shoal stretch to evade Sarn's cutter, the hull groaning the whole way. Beat: terror and exhilaration; the crew functions as a crew for the first time.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Mara. They shelter in a flooded oxbow beside the Meridian, the boat her old crew died on. Mara walks the wreck and retrieves a nameplate she's avoided for seven years. Beat: mourning finally faced; memory stops being a wound and becomes a compass.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The dry season arrives early; the Kestrel grounds on a falling bar with Vessel's Rest still four days' walk upstream. Mara must leave her boat — her whole identity — stranded. Beat: loss of the last refuge; nothing left to hide behind.

chapters.title: Four Days' Walk
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. The three carry the chest's contents overland, hunted by Sarn's men, and Tomas takes a knife wound covering Odile. Beat: sacrifice; Tomas begins paying down his debt in blood.

chapters.title: The Tribunal at Vessel's Rest
chapters.summary: POV Mara. They reach the tribunal as it adjourns for the season; the clerk who could reopen the case is Sarn's old colleague. Mara realizes the chest alone proves nothing without a living witness. Beat: institutional walls; truth needs courage attached.

chapters.title: Sarn in the Marble Hall
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Sarn appears at the tribunal as a respected witness and offers to testify that the chest is Mara's forgery. Tomas, recognizing the archivist's seal-work only he could authenticate, realizes he is the missing witness. Beat: the trap closes and opens in the same breath.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Tomas testifies, exposing his own silence as part of the record; Mara follows, naming her dead crew aloud for the first time. Sarn's forged counter-seal unravels under Tomas's expert reading. Beat: climax — truth spoken at full cost, loyalty redefined as honesty.

chapters.title: The Verdict and the Fire
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Sarn's agents torch the riverfront to destroy remaining records; in the chaos Sarn flees, and Mara chooses to save the tribunal's clerk rather than chase him. Beat: costly victory; justice served imperfectly, heroism chosen over vengeance.

chapters.title: Pardon
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The tribunal grants Mara a full pardon and impounds the chest as evidence. She is legally free — and the Kestrel is still grounded, likely beyond repair. Beat: hollow triumph; freedom arrives with nothing left to be free for.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Tomas buys back the grounded Kestrel at salvage price with his archivist's pension; he and Odile re-caulk her over six weeks of dry-season work. Beat: quiet repair; the boat, like Mara, is declared lost and refuses to be.

chapters.title: A Provision for the Trail
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The Kestrel floats again on rising rains. At the dock, Mara packs provisions for the trail — and, for the first time in seven years, also unpacks a trunk, taking a room she means to return to. Beat: resolution; stopping no longer costs everything, and the river will still be there tomorrow.
